transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Another one breathing. That's already better than most who reach this square.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You were watching before I saw you.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Watching is how you stay alive here. Speak softer if you plan to keep breathing.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Are the houses listening?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Always. They sit in the dark and wait for noise, fear, or a name spoken too loudly.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then I will keep my voice small. But I still need answers.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Everyone who arrives here thinks answers will help them.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Sometimes they do.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Forty years ago I believed that too. I stepped into this square and stopped walking. The fountain is the only place they hesitate to touch.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Forty years standing beside the same stone?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Forty years staying unnoticed. Survival is a quiet skill.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: The shapes in the windows… they felt like judges.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Jinn. Old ones. They rank themselves by how close they dare sit to the oil.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: And someone sits above them all.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Say it softly. There is a king — ancient, between fire and will. Everything here bends toward him eventually.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I passed a woman at the gate who never blinked.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: His daughter. Don't go back to her — whatever she read in your face when you passed, she is still holding it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then the well has a sense of humor.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: No humor. Only appetite.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: The bubbling oil… there are pale hands inside.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Don't count them and don't name them. The pool hollowed them out slowly — there is nothing left in those hands that remembers being a person.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then I should say this before it fades. My brother Omar was dragged here. I dared him to mock the well.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: And a hand answered.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: That means he was noticed. The king chooses carefully — Omar is kept, not lost.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then he is still somewhere in this dark.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Somewhere the king can see him.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Is there anything here the dark fears?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: There is a light. When it is called, the hands sink and the watchers grow quiet.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Quiet sounds useful.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: It is not victory. Only a breath to move.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: A breath is enough.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Using it is like lighting a flare in a cave. Everything will know where you stand.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: If I am already here, hiding isn't much of a strategy.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: That confidence will either save you or make the jinn laugh.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Probably both.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: My hands shake when I reach for the words. The square listens.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then speak them once and let the square hear.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break. Say it once.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Do not repeat it. The square listens for echoes. There is one more. Harder to give.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm listening.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Prayer for the lost: Light find my hand. Light find my path. Let the Sword of Light answer, and let it fade when the shadows loosen. Never say it twice in the same dark.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: First words to hold myself. Second when the hands reach.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Exactly. Use the light only when they touch you. Fear is constant here — the hands are the signal.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: And if the dark speaks with Omar's voice?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Walk past it. The dark has been practicing that longer than you have been alive.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Someone has to be calm down here.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Take my name back to the sun if you escape. Tell them Hanash stood beside the fountain.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I will.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Good. Now go before the houses decide to open their doors.
